subject: Clarify: hosted console export controls & DPA wording
messages:
From: Samuel Green <sam.green@acme.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on data export controls in hosted console

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Two quick questions from our compliance team before we move to procurement: 

1) In the Hosted Console you show an "Export Data" control. Can you confirm what types of customer data are covered by this control (logs, prompts, generated outputs, embeddings)? Our DPA requires explicit export controls per data category.

2) The draft DPA we received lists a cross-border transfer clause that references subprocessors and standard contractual clauses generically. Can you point me to the specific subprocessors handling token logs and any EU data export safeguards (SCCs, EU adequacy reliance)? 

If helpful, I can share our compliance checklist. We just need short public-facing language we can put in our vendor review doc. Appreciate a simple plain-language snippet we can quote to our security team.

Best,
Sam
Samuel Green
Procurement Manager, Acme Corp

Hi all — drafting the public-facing snippet below. I kept it short and explicit so your security reviewer can paste it into their vendor form.

"Redwood Hosted Console — Export controls and covered data: The console’s 'Export Data' function allows customers to export artifacts they create or submit directly (prompts, uploaded files, and generated outputs such as model completions and embeddings). Operational logs (e.g., routing, system telemetry) are retained separately for service reliability and incident investigation; customers may request export or deletion per their DPA rights. Logs containing customer content are only retained when necessary for debugging and with customer consent or as contractually permitted."

Notes for legal: I used the phrase "operational logs" to separate telemetry from customer content. Sam — let me know if you want the snippet shortened further or split into bullet points.

Attaching a doc with two short variants (plain and legal-ready).

Thanks,
Laura
Product Manager, Redwood Console
attachments: console_privacy_snippets_v2.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Samuel Green <sam.green@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on data export controls in hosted console

Thanks Laura — good starting point. A couple of legal clarifications and a DPA redline attached. High-level: 

- Subprocessors: token cache and telemetry are handled by two providers (EdgeStore Inc. and CloudTelemetry Ltd.). EdgeStore holds transient tokenized caches for active inference; CloudTelemetry holds aggregated metrics. Both are covered under our DPA and are in the subprocessor list published in our privacy center.
- Transfers: For EU customer data we rely on SCCs with our subprocessors and an EU data residency option for enterprise customers. We do not rely on a unilateral adequacy declaration for non-technical logs; SCCs are the baseline.
- Exportable items: confirm that customer-generated outputs, prompts, and uploaded artifacts are exportable via the console. Token logs are considered operational and require an access request under the DPA; we can offer a separate export workflow for sensitive customers.

Two action items: 1) Laura — update the public snippet to mention SCCs as the transfer mechanism for EU exports (short line), 2) Sofia/Vivek — confirm whether EdgeStore persists tokenized logs beyond 30 days (I think 7–30 day window depending on config).

Attaching: DPA_export_section_redline.pdf

Kimberly Park
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarification on data export controls in hosted console

Hi Sam — following up with the consolidated response and a very short public-facing copy you can use in vendor review. See below and attached files.

Public snippet (one line, vendor-friendly):
"Redwood Hosted Console allows customers to export customer-created artifacts (prompts, uploaded files, generated outputs and embeddings). Operational telemetry and token caches are managed by subprocessors under signed SCCs; export or deletion of operational logs is available by request per the DPA for customers with contractual access."

Key points in plain language: 
- What can you export: prompts, uploads, completions, embeddings.
- What is operational: token caches and telemetry used for reliability and debugging; these are retained per configured retention windows and require an access request.
- Transfers and subprocessors: EdgeStore Inc. and CloudTelemetry Ltd. process operational data; we use SCCs for EU transfers and offer an EU residency option for enterprise commitments.

Attachments: console_privacy_snippets_v2.docx (2 short variants), DPA_export_section_redline.pdf (legal redline).

Sam — if this looks ok, we can add the one-line snippet to our public privacy center page and I’ll share a short FAQ entry for your security reviewers. If you need signed confirmation of SCC coverage, Kimberly can route a certified subprocessor list.

Thanks,
Sofia
Head of Product — Console
Redwood Inference
